name: accordion
title: Accordion
lead: Build exclusive or independent disclosure groups with native details and summary elements.

variants.title: Exclusive native groups
variants.description: Matching name attributes create native exclusivity. No Collapse classes, controls or JavaScript are required; names must be distinct between separate examples.

variants.title: Independent panels
variants.description: Omit name to keep multiple panels open. Native details supports this directly, rather than through a separate always-open plugin.

variants.title: Nested native groups
variants.description: Use a different name for each level so parent and child exclusivity remain independent.

keyboard.behavior: Focus native summaries and enabled interactive panel content in DOM order.
Toggle the focused native summary; the browser exposes its expanded state.

guidelines: Use native details with a first-child summary, a visible label and an optional aria-hidden decorative chevron.
Matching name values provide exclusivity; omit name for independent panels and use distinct values for nested groups and separate examples.
Do not add redundant button roles, aria-expanded, Collapse data attributes or accordion-button/accordion-collapse compatibility classes.
Listen for the native toggle event or set the details open property in application code. There is no Accordion JavaScript plugin.
Expand-all application code must remove exclusive name grouping before opening every panel; close panels before restoring their shared name.
Panel interpolation is a progressive enhancement. Unsupported browsers toggle immediately; reduced-motion behavior remains native/CSS-driven.
Keep critical instructions available and test native keyboard and assistive-technology behavior.

example:
Account settings
Update your profile and notification preferences.
Security settings
Review password and passkey controls.
javascript: Accordion uses native details and summary elements, the open property and the native toggle event. There is no Accordion JavaScript plugin and no Collapse dependency.

name: collapse
title: Collapse
lead: Toggle content regions with CSS-owned transitions and Collapse JavaScript.

variants.title: Disclosure
variants.description: Collapse changes show and synchronizes trigger aria-expanded. Padding belongs on inner content, not on the animated wrapper.
variants.markup: Project ownership and delivery status.

variants.title: Initially open
variants.description: The constructor preserves authored state. Add show and an initially expanded trigger; no automatic constructor toggle option is required.
variants.markup: This panel starts open.

variants.title: Horizontal collapse
variants.description: The CSS changes inline-size and display. A fixed inline size is set on the immediate child; the outer minimum height is a documentation layout choice.
variants.markup: A compact horizontal panel.

variants.title: Multiple controls and targets
variants.description: Individual controls and a selector-list control can operate the same targets. ARIA controls names every target; no extra styling hook class is invented.
variants.markup:
First target.
Second target.

variants.title: Parent coordination
variants.description: Set parent on target panels. First-level siblings coordinate; this is a Collapse feature, not the native Accordion component.
variants.markup:
Account preferences.
Notification preferences.

variants.title: Independent nested collapse
variants.description: Nested panel state is independent of outer sibling coordination. Closing an ancestor hides its contents without inventing a nested-state reset.
variants.markup:
Nested content.
Second outer panel.

variants.title: Dark mode and RTL
variants.description: The logical animation axis and native button semantics remain unchanged in a local dark RTL region.
variants.markup: The project is ready for review.

keyboard.behavior: Activate a focused native disclosure button. Collapse adds no optional accordion arrow-key policy.
Follow enabled triggers and visible content. Applications manage focus if they hide the currently focused region.

guidelines: Use native type=button triggers with matching targets, aria-controls and initial aria-expanded state.
Collapse adds/removes show only; there is no collapsing transition class or collapsed-trigger class synchronization in this pin.
Keep padding on inner content; horizontal collapse needs an explicit child inline size.
show and hide start events are cancelable; shown/hidden notify after the transition callback. Await completion before dependent operations; calls during a transition are ignored rather than queued.
Parent belongs to the target. Shared triggers can open multiple targets; nested panels retain their own state.
The constructor preserves authored state. Configure parent if needed and call show/hide/toggle explicitly; these methods return completion promises.
Size interpolation is progressive enhancement, with immediate fallback where unsupported. Verify reduced motion and do not hide critical instructions by default.

example: Additional project details.

events.show.trm.collapse: Before adding show; cancel this event to keep the panel closed.
events.shown.trm.collapse: After the show transition callback; a completion notification, not a cancelable start event.
events.hide.trm.collapse: Before removing show; cancel this event to keep the panel open.
events.hidden.trm.collapse: After the hide transition callback; arrange application focus if needed.
